license.notice:
Lingonberry Japanese meaning corrections, edition 4.0.0.

English and Korean definitions were adjudicated against licensed lexical sources and edited with AI assistance. This is not native-speaker certification. Corrections and new Korean translations adapted from Wiktionary/NIKL retain CC BY-SA 4.0 and per-entry source, history and snapshot references. Original source provenance remains preserved in the immutable earlier packages and correction ledger. Retired concepts do not transfer mastery to replacement entries. No audio or third-party quotations are imported. Corrected original usage examples and translations are Lingonberry contributor text under CC BY 4.0; unchanged examples retain their earlier provenance.

Sources credited in this correction edition: English Wiktionary contributors; Japanese Wiktionary contributors; Korean Wiktionary contributors; National Institute of Korean Language. Wiktionary definition text retains CC BY-SA 4.0; NIKL source text retains CC BY-SA 2.0 KR. Article and contributor-history URLs, source snapshot identifiers and selected senses are retained in each correction record.

Earlier source notices:

Learn Language example expansion, edition 3.0.0.

Original examples and translations by Learn Language contributors, 2026, CC BY 4.0. These are AI-assisted editorial drafts; fluent-speaker review remains pending. Sense, article and grammatical corrections to licensed dictionary entries are CC BY-SA 4.0 adaptations. Stable entry IDs and original source provenance are retained. The authoring and correction records are included in language-packages/sources/examples/. No unreviewed model output, audio or publisher quotations are added.

Earlier edition source notices follow:

Learn Language multilingual dictionaries, edition 2.0.0 (editorial preview).

Korean Learners' Dictionary (한국어기초사전), National Institute of Korean Language (국립국어원): Korean headwords, definitions, translated equivalents/definitions and Korean sentence examples. Original text licence: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 2.0 Korea. Source: https://krdict.korean.go.kr/ . Copyright policy: https://krdict.korean.go.kr/kor/kboardPolicy/copyRightTermsInfo . Licence: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/kr/ . Each imported entry retains its source entry and sense identifiers and direct source URL. XML export dated 19 June 2026, redistributed by spellcheck-ko/korean-dict-nikl at commit 42c0d01889f34536e9cf94fe57f62bd2055b1bde.

Adaptations by Learn Language contributors: reorganising bilingual equivalents into study-language headwords, selecting senses, adding editorial levels and topic tags, normalising forms and linking lexical facts. Adaptations are offered under CC BY-SA 4.0, using the later same-elements licence option in section 4(2) of the original Korean licence. Unmodified source text retains its original licence. Native-speaker review is pending; no official exam membership or dictionary-provider endorsement is claimed.

English Wiktionary contributors: grammatical facts and contributor-authored usage examples extracted via Kaikki/Wiktextract. Text licence CC BY-SA 4.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ . Each reused item retains the source article URL and contributor-history URL. Quotation-type examples, attributed quotations, images and audio are excluded. Source translations present in the extract are identified as source English translations, not newly reviewed translations. https://kaikki.org/dictionary/rawdata.html

National Institute of Korean Language, 2017 International Standard Curriculum for the Korean Language (vocabulary spreadsheet revised 2020): headword grade evidence, under Korea Open Government Licence Type 1 (attribution). https://www.korean.go.kr/front/reportData/reportDataView.do?mn_id=207&report_seq=932 . Curriculum grades are not exhaustive TOPIK exam word lists; homograph matches are headword-level evidence only.

The original 1.0.0 starter definitions and bilingual examples remain CC BY 4.0, Learn Language contributors, 2026: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ . They are preserved with their stable identifiers. App code remains MIT.

Keep source credits, licence links, contributor-history links and modification notices when redistributing. ShareAlike applies to covered adapted content; the app's independently written code has its own licence. Data JSON is provided separately without DRM through the repository download links. Do not apply extra contractual or technical restrictions to the licensed data. No external speech recordings are bundled; speech uses device voices. Store-distribution compliance and language review remain release checks, not completed certifications.

Complete bilingual example coverage has not been achieved. Untranslated native source examples are labelled separately and are excluded from sentence quizzes. No generic repeated topic sentence is counted as a completed usage example.

Wordfreq 3.1.1, Robyn Speer and contributors: frequency estimates used for editorial ordering, not exam membership. Code is Apache-2.0; distributed frequency data is CC BY-SA 4.0. See https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq for the source-data acknowledgements and https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ . Frequency is a historic usage estimate and does not establish the difficulty of a specific sense.

Wordfreq source acknowledgements: Google Books Ngrams and Syntactic Ngrams; University of Leeds Centre for Translation Studies Internet Corpus; Wikipedia contributors; ParaCrawl; OPUS/OpenSubtitles 2018 and the OpenSubtitles project; SUBTLEX-US, UK, CH, DE and NL authors including Brysbaert, New, Buchmeier, Conrad, Jacobs, Bölte, Böhl, Cai, Keuleers, van Heuven, Mandera and colleagues. SUBTLEX remains freely available at https://crr.ugent.be/programs-data/subtitle-frequencies . Full upstream citations: https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq#citations-to-work-that-wordfreq-is-built-on . retiredEntries.reason: The cached Japanese lexical sense is animal flesh, not fruit flesh. Replace the imported fruit concept and align the example.
The imported spending-plan concept is not Japanese 規模; replace it with the attested scale/extent concept.
The imported highest-minister title of Goryeo or Joseon is not the selected Japanese concept; replace it with the attested modern government-head sense.
The explosive fuse definition belongs to 導火線; 芯 supports wick, a different selected concept.
The Korean legal cultural-heritage designation is not the ordinary Japanese meaning of 宝物.
The imported wholesale-only definition describes a wholesaler; Japanese ディーラー is the broader dealer concept.
家計 denotes household finances, not the family as an economic unit.
台無し means ruined or spoiled, not merely untidy or complicated.
一層 is a comparative intensifier here, not continuous addition.
The original details describe Korean gyeongdan/tteok and its toppings, not Japanese dango.
味付け denotes the action or resulting flavour, not the seasoning ingredient 調味料.
The Korean source transferred Seoul; Japanese 上京 normally refers to Tokyo, historically Kyoto.
The thirty-year meteorological normal is 平年; 例年 is usual years, a different reference concept.
The original medical/sleep eye-mask restriction is not the ordinary 目隠し blindfold concept.
胃腸 names the organs, not the abdominal space containing them.
The source noun 鉢 denotes the vessel, not the Korean bowlful counting-unit concept.
安置 is placing or laying in repose, not burial or cremation itself.
The Joseon crown-prince-specific definition is a Korean cultural transfer; Japanese 殿下 is not limited to that referent.
下水 is wastewater, not the bottom of a pool of stagnant water.
The imported mental-peace sense does not match Japanese 和平 ending hostilities.
冤罪 denotes the false accusation/conviction, not the resulting bad reputation.
A topic is the subject, not a story’s title.
The Korean former-king honorific is not the Japanese 大王 concept.
The checked Japanese noun denotes the dance venue, not any freestyle dance.
Being younger than oneself is not a sense of 小人; select the supported child sense and its reading しょうにん. しょうじん denotes a mean or narrow-minded person.
Stopping sweat production is not the same action as 冷やす cooling something.
A person’s family ancestry is not the selected Japanese 根幹 foundation sense.
The original Korean campus-worship meeting sense differs from the checked Japanese chapel building sense.
空く is not the loss of personal wealth or becoming empty-handed.
The Korean grouping of secondary schools under an entrance-exam system differs from the Japanese attendance-area concept.
Original reading カムジュ and the Korean barley-malt rice drink describe gamju/sikhye, not Japanese 甘酒.
The ordinary Japanese 巻物 is not a roll of toilet paper.
Imported becoming morally bad definition does not match the selected Japanese verb; use attested err sense.
Day employment does not inherently mean an unskilled person or derogatory label.
Imported feeling of displeasure is not the adjective’s meaning.
Spare means devote or allocate here, not save resources.
Plot outline is not the detailed dialogue script imported here.
Financial portfolio denotes assets themselves, not detailed information about them.
Hard worker is not merely a person assigned responsibility.
Korean academic rank definition does not match historical Japanese rank.
Projection onto an object is not transmission through it.
Korean Joseon title and transcription mismatch Japanese ancient Chinese title.
Imported definition describes a dash rather than a hyphen.
Imported displeasure state is not absurd/foolish adjective.
Share of something is not a duty assigned by turn.
Literal heart blood is unsupported; attested Japanese concept is all one’s energy.
Imported liquid or energy surge is not this surprise adverb.
Flag emblem or declared cause is not the flag itself.
Imported reclamation by draining water differs from clearing land for cultivation.
Manipulating someone is not intransitive playing or flirting.
Pioneer starts a field rather than merely understanding life earlier.
Last-place person or rank is not the physical end of an object.
Japanese bide specifically denotes genital/front washing rather than anal washing.
Divine talent is mismatched; Japanese word is a sovereign’s gift.
Civil official is not specifically civilian employee of the military.
Harvesting or mowing differs from pruning side shoots.
Imported Korean yakbap recipe differs from general Japanese steamed glutinous rice.
Deliberately does not mean concealing one’s intention.
亥年 denotes the year, not the personal zodiac sign of someone born in it.
弦月 is a half-moon, not the crescent phase described by the imported meaning.
A coffee pot is not an electric kettle for boiling water.
脱漏 denotes omission, not physically taking something outside.
霜焼け denotes chilblains, not freezing and necrosis from frostbite.
お化け屋敷 means a haunted house, not simply a house whose occupants have bad luck.
一人 is a count of one person, not a generic unspecified thing or person.
丸っ切り expresses degree or totality, not the concessive no-matter-how-one-tries meaning.
